name: math_occupancy
kind: do instruction classes bound to different execution units share one SMSP issue path; 16 warps per SMSP; no workload-based fitting
question: When the warps of an SMSP interleave instructions of two classes that the tree binds to different units (IMAD on fmaheavy, LOP3 / FMNMX on alu, FADD on fma), does one instruction cost what a single-class stream costs (shared path: interval sum) or less (separate units run in parallel)? And does c = interval x W continue to 16 warps per SMSP?
probe: math_occupancy.cu extended: (1) mixed streams of 256 instructions alternating two classes, all independent (rotating destinations, loop-invariant sources): imad_lop3, imad_fadd (independent FADD, not a chain), lop3_fadd, imad_imadhi (mul.hi), fadd_fmul; plus the single-class independent streams fadd_ind and imadhi as references. (2) --ctas C (1 or 2): C CTAs of 32 x 4 x W threads on the same SM (the second CTA is placed by launching a grid of C x SM-count CTAs and letting only the CTAs whose %smid equals the SM of CTA 0 take part, as the row_gather sweep does; the others exit at once), all participants start on a global counter, so W = 8 with C = 2 gives 16 warps per SMSP. Cells: streams (7 + imad, lop3 from v1) x W in {4, 8} x C in {1, 2}, placement four SMSPs; 33 reps x 8 launches; runs a and b.

controls.sass: between the clock reads exactly 128 + 128 instructions of the two declared opcodes strictly alternating (256 for single streams), no memory, no branch.
controls.timing: v1 cells imad / lop3 at W = 4, 8, C = 1 reproduce v1 within 5 %; runs a and b agree within 5 %; with C = 2 the number of participating warps per SMSP is recorded from %smid / warp id and must be 2 x W.

predictions_before_data.shared_path: if the classes share one issue path per SMSP: c(mixed) = W x (i_a + i_b) / 2 with the single-stream intervals i (IMAD 2, IMAD.HI ?, LOP3 2, FADD 1, FMUL 1): imad_lop3 = 2.0 x W, imad_fadd = 1.5 x W, lop3_fadd = 1.5 x W.
predictions_before_data.separate_units: if units are independent (engine today): c(mixed) = W x max(i_a, i_b) / 2 -> imad_lop3 = 1.0 x W, imad_fadd = 1.0 x W (the front end's 1 per cycle is the floor: W x 1.0).
predictions_before_data.w16: C = 2 cells: c doubles against C = 1 (c = interval x 16).

outcomes_before_data.shared: If mixed cells follow the shared-path prediction within 10 %: the per-class issue interval is charged on the SMSP issue front end (one path), not on separate units; engine rule: an instruction occupies the SMSP issue front end for its class interval (structural field on the front-end resource), units keep max_inflight roles only. No new values.
outcomes_before_data.separate: If they follow the separate-unit prediction: engine is right; the dropout deficit is elsewhere.
outcomes_before_data.other: Otherwise report the table; addendum before any install.

prediction_check: H100 replay of imad_lop3 and imad_fadd at W = 8, C = 1: c within 15 %; then the full-gpu regression against fg-over20/full-g1.
not_allowed: No family / case / shape specific timing; no tuning to the full-gpu error; post-data changes are labelled.

addenda.runs: $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/microbench/math_occupancy/h100-v2r3 (52 + 52 rows, SASS gate passed, strict alternation)
addenda.text: Probe form changed before the run that counts: ptxas reorders independent instructions and fuses FADD + FMUL, so the mixed streams are serial chains alternating the two classes (each instruction reads the previous destination; -fmad=false), with single-class chains as references. Cycles per instruction and warp at W = 4 / 8 per SMSP, one CTA: imad 7.59 / 15.96, lop3 7.59 / 15.57, imadhi 15.93 / 31.57, fmul_chain 4.03 / 7.85, fadd_ind 1.02 / 1.02; mixed: imad_lop3 7.98 / 15.77 (2.0 x W), imad_fadd 5.95 / 11.41 (1.5 x W), lop3_fadd 6.49 / 11.85 (1.5 x W), imad_imadhi 12.41 / 24.72 (3.1 x W), fadd_fmul 4.04 / 7.87 (1.0 x W). Prediction shared_path HOLDS (within 10 %): instructions of classes bound to different units share one issue path per SMSP and each occupies it for its class interval (IMAD 2, LOP3 2, IMAD.HI 4, FADD / FMUL 1); c(mixed) = W x mean interval. The separate-unit prediction (1.0 x W for imad_lop3 and imad_fadd) is rejected. Prediction w16 FAILED: with two CTAs on the SM (8 / 16 warps per SMSP) c stays within 10 % of the one-CTA value (imad 8.41 / 16.71); not explained, not modelled. Install (structural, no new value): an instruction occupies the SMSP issue front end for its class issue interval; the per-class units no longer carry the interval.

addenda.when: after the engine replay and the full-gpu regression of the rule declared in the previous addendum (2026-11-14); corrections
addenda.text: (1) The install of the previous addendum is WITHDRAWN. scheduler.shared_issue_path was implemented for every class with an SMSP unit; the probe measured IMAD, IMAD.HI, LOP3, FADD and FMUL only. Replay ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/fg-over20/mocc-replay-table.txt, W = 8, one CTA): the engine gives the same c with the rule on and off (imad 15.84, imad_lop3 16.18, imad_fadd 12.35 against hardware 15.96 / 15.77 / 11.41), i.e. the engine already reproduced these chain cells before the rule (the previous addendum's sentence 'the separate-unit prediction is what the engine does' was an assumption and is wrong for chains), so the replay does not support the change. In full-gpu jobs the rule lets a MUFU (interval 8.26), a conversion or a matrix instruction hold the path for its whole interval against every other class of the SMSP (fa3_fwd_mask_09: FMNMX 4.4 -> 10.2, FADD 1.8 -> 6.8, HGMMA 9.2 -> 37.4 cycles per issue); no cell measured that. The h100 leaf stays 0 (field and code are not merged). (2) The statement 'w16 FAILED: two CTAs do not add' is wrong: the C = 2 cells are bimodal (imad W = 8: p10 3496, p50 4278, p90 8429 cycles per window; imadhi 8078 / 8253 / 16564): the warps of one CTA finish in the one-CTA time and the warps of the other in twice that. The SM-level rate is the single-unit rate for 16 warps per SMSP; the service order is CTA after CTA rather than interleaved. The table's median hides this. (3) What stands from v2: single-class cells and the pair sums as measured facts; among them imad_imadhi = 3.1 x W with IMAD 2.0 x W and IMAD.HI 4.0 x W alone - the two classes take turns on one multiplier (separate units would give 2.0 x W). The tree binds IMAD to fmaheavy_smsp and IMAD.HI to issue_frontend_smsp. Next check, declared here before it is run: replay imad_imadhi, imadhi and imad at W = 8, one CTA, with the present tree and with IMAD.HI bound to fmaheavy_smsp (interval unchanged, 4.005); install the binding only if imad_imadhi comes within 15 % of 24.7 with it and is outside without it, and the other two cells do not move by more than 5 %.

addenda.when: after the first A / B replay of the IMAD.HI binding (2026-11-14); check re-declared before it is re-run
addenda.text: The check of the previous addendum could not discriminate, for a reason found in the replay: on Hopper the class IMAD.HI is unreachable. cpp/arch/hopper/convert_rules.cpp and python/cyclescope/arch/hopper/rules.py return the opcode root IMAD for IMAD.HI (Blackwell has the IMAD + HI branch), so every IMAD.HI is served by the IMAD leaf (interval 2.006) and the installed Hopper leaf instruction.service .. operation_class=IMAD.HI (interval 4.005, result 9.0, service_latency.h100.r3s) is never used. Replay of the independent imadhi stream at W = 8: engine 15.87 cycles per instruction (issues 2 cycles apart on the SMSP in the journal), hardware 31.57. $CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/fg-over20/mulhi-replay-table.txt; its fixcls columns are void (the journal of that run shows the same class ids as the unfixed run: the classification change had not reached the facts). Re-declared check: (0) add the IMAD + HI -> IMAD.HI branch to both Hopper classifiers (parity with Blackwell; no leaf value changes) and verify in the journal that the 256 IMAD.HI instances carry a class different from IMAD; (1) with it, imadhi must come within 15 % of 31.57 and imad stay within 5 % of its present 15.94 - then the classification fix is installed on that evidence alone; (2) imad_imadhi (hardware 24.72): with the tree as it is (IMAD.HI on issue_frontend_smsp) and with IMAD.HI bound to fmaheavy_smsp; the binding is changed only if the present tree is outside 15 % and the re-bound tree inside; if both are inside nothing more is changed, if both are outside the result is reported and the binding left alone.

Result ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/fg-over20/mulhi-replay2-table.txt; W = 8, one CTA; cycles per instruction, engine with the tree as it was | with IMAD.HI on fmaheavy_smsp | hardware): imad 15.94 | 15.94 | 15.96; imadhi 31.75 | 31.77 | 31.57; imad_imadhi 15.96 | 23.91 | 24.72. Journal: the IMAD.HI instances now carry their own class (issues 4 cycles apart per SMSP, 2 before the classifier fix). Both criteria met as declared: the Hopper classifiers return IMAD.HI (the installed leaf becomes reachable), and IMAD.HI is bound to the multiplier unit fmaheavy_smsp it shares with IMAD (source math_occupancy.h100.v2r3, experimental). Blackwell is unchanged (its probe run stopped at the SASS gate: max.f32 compiles to FMNMX3 there; its IMAD.HI binding is unmeasured).
